# Pawpath Online Rebooking — Product Requirements Document

**Author:** [account name from CLI context] | **Date:** October 15, 2026 | **Status:** Draft v1.0 | **Review by:** TBD

---

Pawpath's reminder workflow breaks down at the finish line: 31% of patients due for a recheck never rebook, costing clinics revenue and compromising patient outcomes, while front-desk staff burn roughly 6 hours per week on manual reminder calls. This PRD defines a one-tap online rebooking flow—triggered from SMS and email reminders and wired into the existing Pawpath calendar service—that eliminates the phone-call requirement. Success is defined as raising recheck rebooking from 69% to 80% within two quarters and reducing per-clinic reminder-call overhead from 6 hours to 2 hours per week, with beta delivery in 10 weeks across 12 pilot clinics.

---

## Problem Statement

### Observed Friction
- **31%** of patients due for a recheck never schedule the follow-up visit
- Rebooking currently requires a phone call — a synchronous, high-friction step that many pet owners defer or skip
- Front-desk staff spend **~6 hours per week per clinic** on outbound reminder calls, diverting them from in-clinic patient care

### Why It Matters
- Missed rechecks represent direct revenue loss for independent clinics (Assumption: average recheck revenue per visit TBD — pilot clinics should surface this figure)
- Patient health outcomes worsen when follow-up care is skipped (e.g., post-surgery checks, medication adjustments)
- Staff time spent on calls is an operational cost that scales poorly as clinic appointment volume grows

### PM Gap Identified
No data was provided on **why** owners don't rebook (scheduling inconvenience vs. cost vs. forgetting). Recommendation: add a 3-question exit survey to the rebooking flow during beta to capture abandonment reasons for future iteration.

---

## Target Users & Personas

### Persona 1 — Maya, the Busy Pet Owner
- **Context:** Dog had a skin condition recheck scheduled; receives an SMS reminder 5 days out
- **Device:** Smartphone (74% of Pawpath reminder opens are on mobile)
- **Pain point:** Calling the clinic during work hours is inconvenient; she delays and forgets
- **Need:** Book a time in under 60 seconds without a phone call

### Persona 2 — Jordan, Front-Desk Coordinator
- **Context:** Works at a 4-vet independent clinic; manages scheduling alongside check-ins and checkout
- **Pain point:** Spends ~6 hours/week calling patients who often don't answer, requiring 2–3 callback attempts
- **Need:** Fewer inbound scheduling calls and clear visibility into which patients have self-rebooked vs. still need outreach

---

## Goals & Success Metrics

| Goal | Metric | Baseline | Target | Window |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Increase recheck rebooking | % of due-for-recheck patients who book | 69% | **80%** | 2 quarters post-launch |
| Reduce staff call time | Reminder-call hours per clinic/week | 6 hrs | **2 hrs** | 2 quarters post-launch |
| Mobile conversion | % of SMS/email link opens that complete booking | Assumption: establish in beta | Target: ≥ 40% | Beta (10 weeks) |
| Booking completion speed | Median time from reminder open to confirmed booking | Assumption: establish in beta | Target: < 90 seconds | Beta (10 weeks) |

---

## Detailed Requirements

### Functional Requirements

#### FR-1: One-Tap Rebooking Link
- Reminder SMS and email must contain a unique, tokenized deep-link per patient per recheck
- Link must pre-populate: patient name, pet name, appointment type (recheck), and attending vet
- Owner confirms or changes the pre-filled slot — no login required for the core flow

#### FR-2: Slot Selection UI
- Display available slots from the existing Pawpath calendar service (real-time)
- Mobile-first layout; must be fully functional on a 375 px viewport
- Show at minimum 5 available slots across the next 14 days, grouped by day
- Allow owner to select a different vet if preferred vet has no availability within 7 days

#### FR-3: Booking Confirmation
- On slot selection, send an instant confirmation SMS + email with appointment details and a one-tap cancellation link
- Write the confirmed appointment back to the Pawpath calendar service via existing API
- Display a clinic-specific confirmation message (configurable by clinic admin)

#### FR-4: Staff Dashboard Signal
- Front-desk view in Pawpath must show a "Self-Rebooked" status on patient records updated within the last 48 hours
- Aggregate weekly report: total reminders sent, self-rebook rate, still-pending count — auto-emailed to clinic admin every Monday

#### FR-5: Fallback & Escalation
- If zero slots are available in the next 14 days, show a "Request a time" form (name + phone + preferred window) that generates a staff task in Pawpath
- If token is expired (Assumption: 7-day token TTL — validate with eng), redirect to clinic phone number

### Non-Functional Requirements

| Category | Requirement |
|---|---|
| **Performance** | Booking link must load in < 2 seconds on a 4G connection |
| **Availability** | Target: 99.5% uptime during clinic hours (Assumption: 7am–8pm local time) |
| **Security** | Tokens must be single-use or time-limited; no PHI exposed in URL parameters |
| **Accessibility** | WCAG 2.1 AA compliance on the booking UI |
| **Scalability** | Must support all 12 pilot clinics concurrently in beta without degradation |
| **Calendar Integrity** | Zero double-bookings; all writes must go through the existing Pawpath calendar service with idempotency keys |

---

## User Stories & Acceptance Criteria

**US-1 — Pet Owner: Rebook from SMS**
> *As a pet owner, I want to tap a link in my reminder text and book a recheck slot without calling the clinic.*
- **AC:** Given I tap the SMS link, I see pre-filled pet and appointment info within 2 seconds
- **AC:** Given I select a slot and confirm, I receive a confirmation text within 30 seconds
- **AC:** The appointment appears in the clinic's Pawpath calendar immediately

**US-2 — Pet Owner: No Available Slots**
> *As a pet owner, I want an alternative if no slots are shown.*
- **AC:** If no slots exist in 14 days, I see a "Request a callback" form, not a dead end

**US-3 — Front-Desk Staff: Reduced Call Queue**
> *As a front-desk coordinator, I want to know which patients have already self-rebooked so I only call those who haven't.*
- **AC:** Patient list in Pawpath shows "Self-Rebooked" badge with timestamp
- **AC:** I can filter the recheck list by "Pending" vs. "Rebooked" status

**US-4 — Clinic Admin: Weekly Performance Visibility**
> *As a clinic admin, I want a weekly summary of rebooking rates.*
- **AC:** Monday morning email shows: reminders sent, self-booked count, self-book rate %, still-pending count

---

## Scope

### In Scope
- One-tap rebooking via SMS and email reminder links
- Real-time slot display using existing Pawpath calendar service
- Booking confirmation (SMS + email)
- Staff dashboard status signal ("Self-Rebooked")
- Weekly admin email report
- Fallback "request a callback" form

### Out of Scope
- **Payments** (explicitly excluded)
- New calendar service or scheduling engine (must reuse existing)
- Multi-pet household booking in a single flow (Assumption: defer to v2)
- In-app rebooking (native Pawpath app, if one exists) — beta targets SMS/email only
- New appointment types beyond rechecks

---

## Technical Considerations

- **Token architecture:** Unique per-reminder tokens must encode patient ID, appointment type, and clinic ID without exposing raw database IDs in the URL
- **Calendar API:** Confirm whether the existing Pawpath calendar service supports real-time slot reads and idempotent writes — this is the highest-risk dependency; spike recommended in Week 1
- **Reminder pipeline:** Determine where tokens are injected into existing SMS/email sends — requires coordination with the team owning reminder delivery
- **Double-booking prevention:** Implement optimistic locking or slot reservation (hold for Assumption: 5 minutes) to prevent race conditions when two owners view the same slot
- **Analytics instrumentation:** Add events for: link open, slot viewed, slot selected, booking confirmed, booking abandoned — essential for measuring the mobile conversion target

---

## Risks & Mitigations

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Calendar API can't support required read/write patterns | Medium | High | Week 1 spike; if blocked, negotiate API extension or thin adapter layer |
| Token security flaw exposes patient data | Low | High | Security review before beta; single-use or short-TTL tokens; penetration test on staging |
| Pilot clinics have inconsistent calendar hygiene (stale slots) | High | Medium | Onboarding checklist for pilot clinics; real-time slot refresh, not cached |
| Low SMS link click-through reduces measurable impact | Medium | Medium | A/B test reminder copy in beta; add owner name personalization |
| 10-week timeline is compressed | Medium | High | Scope freeze after kick-off; daily async status update; cut weekly report to v1.1 if needed |

**PM Gap Identified:** No data on current reminder delivery channel mix (SMS vs. email open rates beyond the 74% mobile stat). Recommend pulling delivery analytics before finalizing reminder copy and link placement strategy.

---

## Timeline & Milestones

| Week | Milestone |
|---|---|
| **1** | Calendar API spike complete; token architecture agreed; pilot clinic onboarding starts |
| **2–3** | Core booking UI built (mobile-first); slot read integration |
| **4** | Write-back to calendar + confirmation SMS/email |
| **5** | Staff dashboard "Self-Rebooked" signal; fallback form |
| **6** | End-to-end QA; security review of token system |
| **7** | Staging with 2 internal test clinics; analytics events validated |
| **8** | Beta launch with 12 pilot clinics |
| **9–10** | Beta monitoring; weekly report feature; bug fixes |
| **Q2 end** | Measure 80% rebooking target; go/no-go for general availability |

---

## Prioritized Next Steps

1. **[Week 1 — Blocker]** Run a calendar API spike to confirm real-time slot read/write capability; document any gaps within 5 days
2. **[Week 1 — Blocker]** Agree on token security architecture with engineering; define TTL and PHI handling rules
3. **[Week 1 — High]** Lock pilot clinic list (12 clinics confirmed) and schedule onboarding calls to audit calendar hygiene
4. **[Week 1 — High]** Instrument existing reminder delivery pipeline with open/click analytics to establish mobile conversion baseline
5. **[Week 2 — Medium]** Add a 3-question abandonment micro-survey to the booking flow to capture "why didn't you rebook?" signal for v2
6. **[Before beta — Medium]** Validate average recheck revenue per visit with pilot clinics to quantify the revenue impact of the 11-point rebooking lift
7. **[Ongoing]** Freeze scope at kick-off; any additions go to a v1.1 backlog to protect the 10-week deadline

# Pawpath H2 Clinic Growth

*OKR Set | Fernway Labs — Pawpath | Owner: [account name from CLI context] | Sprint: Oct 15 – Dec 31, 2026*

---

Fernway Labs enters the final 11 weeks of H2 with 410 paying clinics, $1.9M ARR, and a 2.1% monthly logo churn rate that quietly removes an Estimate of ~8–9 clinics every month (Estimate: 2.1% × 410 = 8.6 clinics/month). The three OKRs below attack the highest-leverage problems in sequence: stop the bleeding in the first 90 days, mechanize onboarding to free capacity for higher-ACV deals, and convert that operational discipline into net-new clinic growth — all without a paid acquisition budget increase. Because these OKRs are being set mid-H2, targets are scoped as a focused Q4 sprint; confirm with leadership whether they replace or complement any July commitments already in flight.

---

## OKR 1: Turn the First 90 Days from a Danger Zone into a Loyalty-Building Experience

**Why it matters:** Early churn is the single biggest constraint on ARR growth. Every clinic lost before Day 90 erases acquisition cost and caps the ceiling of the business.

### Key Results

- **KR 1.1** Reduce monthly logo churn from **2.1% to Target: 1.2%** by December 31, 2026, measured by end-of-month active paying clinic count.
- **KR 1.2** Increase 90-day cohort retention (clinics still active 90 days post-activation) to **Target: 85%** — *Assumption: baseline not currently tracked; must be instrumented by Oct 22 or this KR is unmeasurable for H2.*
- **KR 1.3** Achieve a median time-to-first-core-action (clinic logs its first appointment in Pawpath) of **Target: ≤ 5 business days** — *Assumption: not currently measured; requires analytics instrumentation.*
- **KR 1.4** Complete structured exit interviews with **Target: 100%** of clinics that churn in Q4 2026, surfacing the top 3 actionable churn drivers by Dec 15, 2026.

> **⚠️ Coach Flag — KR 1.2 & 1.3:** Both KRs require instrumentation that may not exist. If baselines are not established by Oct 22, these become unscoreable. Prioritize metric plumbing before any roadmap build work begins.

---

## OKR 2: Build a Self-Serve Onboarding Engine That Scales Without Adding Headcount

**Why it matters:** Three onboarding specialists handling every single-clinic activation is a bottleneck with two compounding costs — high cost-per-clinic-onboarded and zero capacity for higher-ACV multi-site group accounts.

### Key Results

- **KR 2.1** Achieve **Target: 65%** of new clinics completing full onboarding (account configured + first user trained + first appointment logged) without any live specialist touchpoint, by Dec 31, 2026 — *Assumption: current self-serve completion rate is near 0%; validate immediately.*
- **KR 2.2** Reduce average specialist time-per-new-clinic from **Assumption: [baseline TBD — measure by Oct 22]** to **Target: ≤ 1.5 hours** by Dec 31, 2026.
- **KR 2.3** Redirect **Target: ≥ 60%** of total onboarding specialist hours toward multi-site group deal support by Dec 31, 2026, tracked via weekly capacity logs.

> **⚠️ Coach Flag — KR 2.1:** 65% self-serve in ~11 weeks is aggressive if no self-serve infrastructure exists today. Engineering must scope a guided setup wizard as the MVP by Oct 18 — if the realistic ship date falls in December, this target may need to shift to H1 2027. Better to right-size than to silently sandbagg.

> **⚠️ Coach Flag — KR 2.3:** "Hours redirected" is a leading indicator, not a business outcome. It is included here to make the capacity shift visible, but it must be paired with KR 3.3 below to confirm the redirect is generating revenue — otherwise it is an output masquerading as a result.

---

## OKR 3: Grow Paying Clinics and ARR Through Retention Gains and Sales Efficiency

**Why it matters:** Without a paid acquisition budget increase, growth must come from two sources: retaining more of what is won and converting freed capacity into higher-ACV multi-site group deals. This OKR captures the business outcome of OKRs 1 and 2 materializing.

### Key Results

- **KR 3.1** Grow paying clinics from **410 to Target: 450** by December 31, 2026.
- **KR 3.2** Grow ARR from **$1.9M to Target: $2.1M** by December 31, 2026 — *Assumption: blended ACV of new single-site clinics holds near the current Estimate of ~$4,634/year ($1.9M ÷ 410); multi-site groups at higher ACV could accelerate this.*

To net 40 clinics and reach 450, approximately 64 new activations are needed — roughly 23/month. If the current new-clinic run rate is below that, this target is unreachable. If it is above that, it may be sandbagged. **Pull the current monthly new-clinic activation number before signing off on this KR** — it is the single most important unknown in this entire OKR set.

---

## Expert Analysis

### Causal Chain Is Correct
The sequencing — fix churn → mechanize onboarding → accelerate growth — is exactly right under Doerr's "less is more" principle. Pouring acquisition dollars into a 2.1% monthly churn bucket is a treadmill. These three OKRs have a clear causal dependency and should be communicated to the team as a chain, not three parallel initiatives.

### Critical Gaps

| Gap | Risk | Action |
|---|---|---|
| **No churn reason data** | KR 1 work is guesswork without it | Start exit interviews this week — contacts go cold fast |
| **Current new-clinic acquisition rate unknown** | KR 3.1 target cannot be validated | Pull from CRM immediately |
| **Multi-site group pipeline unquantified** | KR 3.3 targets are pure assumptions | Sales alignment meeting by Oct 22 |
| **Engineering capacity not scoped** | Self-serve wizard may not ship in 11 weeks | Require scoping before locking OKR 2 |
| **No defined "multi-site group" ICP** | Sales could pursue wrong accounts with freed time | Define ≥ 2 locations + Target: TBD ACV threshold as qualification criteria |

| Presumed Company OKR | Pawpath OKR That Feeds It |
|---|---|
| Grow company ARR to **[company target — TBD]** | OKR 3 (KR 3.1, 3.2, 3.3) |
| Achieve net revenue retention **> 100%** | OKR 1 (churn reduction is the primary driver) |
| Move upmarket toward multi-site and group accounts | OKR 2 unlocks OKR 3's group KRs |
| Reduce cost-to-serve per customer | OKR 2 (self-serve reduces specialist cost per clinic) |

> **Recommendation:** If no company-level OKRs exist, this set effectively *is* the company-level plan. In that case, add a fourth objective owning the multi-site commercial motion explicitly — the current plan assumes group revenue materializes organically from freed capacity, which is too passive a bet to leave unowned.

**By Oct 18 (this week)**
1. **Engineering scoping session** — scope self-serve onboarding wizard MVP; confirm a realistic ship date before KR 2.1's 65% target is locked.
2. **Pull current monthly new-clinic activation rate from CRM** — required to validate or revise KR 3.1.

**By Oct 29 (week 3)**

7. **Publish a shared OKR dashboard** with weekly check-in cadence across product, engineering, and onboarding. Doerr's CFR rhythm (Conversations, Feedback, Recognition) is what makes OKRs live beyond this document.

# Why Clinics Switch to Pawpath
### Jobs-to-be-Done Analysis — Independent Vet Clinics
*Prepared for: Pawpath Product Team | Date: 15 October 2026*

---

Across 8 interviews with clinic managers who switched to Pawpath within the last year, a consistent pattern emerges: independent vet clinics are not primarily buying scheduling software — they are hiring a solution to **reclaim professional dignity and personal time**. The dominant "competitor" is not another SaaS product; it is a patchwork of a paper diary plus a shared spreadsheet, used by 6 of the 8 managers interviewed. Three trigger events repeatedly cause the switch: unrelenting phone volume, a visible double-booking failure in front of a client, and the creep of admin work into evenings. Pawpath's messaging and onboarding must speak to these moments of crisis, not to feature lists.

---

## Functional Jobs

These are the operational tasks clinic managers are trying to accomplish.

### Core Functional Jobs

- **When** the reception desk is overwhelmed with incoming calls, **I want to** let clients self-book online at any hour, **so I can** reduce inbound call volume and keep the desk focused on in-clinic care.

- **When** two staff members update the same appointment slot from different locations, **I want to** have a single, real-time source of truth for availability, **so I can** eliminate double bookings before they reach the client.

- **When** the phone rings for the tenth time in an hour, **I want to** feel confident the booking process is under control, **so I can** stop bracing for the next scheduling crisis.

- **When** a client arrives and there is a scheduling conflict, **I want to** appear organised and in control, **so I can** signal that my clinic is as capable as any larger practice.

- **When** my staff complain about booking chaos, **I want to** be seen as a manager who solves problems decisively, **so I can** maintain authority and team morale.

- **When** a fellow independent clinic owner asks how I manage appointments, **I want to** be the person who has figured it out, **so I can** position myself as a competent operator, not someone still using a paper diary.

What managers use — consciously or not — to evaluate whether a solution deserves the job.

| Criterion | Signal from Interviews |
|---|---|
| **Eliminates double bookings** | "Double bookings embarrassed us" — zero tolerance; a single recurrence disqualifies a tool |
| **Reduces inbound call volume** | "Phones never stopped ringing" — measurable relief expected within weeks of going live |
| **Works outside clinic hours** | "I wanted my evenings back" — 24/7 self-booking is a threshold requirement, not a differentiator |
| **Adoptable by all staff** | Paper + spreadsheet used by 6 of 8 — staff must abandon entrenched habits; friction must be near zero |
| **Trustworthy as a single source** | Dual-system failure (diary + spreadsheet) was the pain source; consolidation into one system is the hire |

### Primary Incumbent (6 of 8 clinics)
**Paper diary + shared spreadsheet** — the dominant prior solution. Not chosen for its quality; inherited by default. Its failure modes (concurrent edits, no mobile access, no client self-service) are the direct cause of switching.

### Secondary Competitors
*(No additional products named in interviews — see Gaps section)*

- **Assumption to validate:** Some clinics may have trialled a competing scheduling SaaS before or alongside the paper/spreadsheet system. This is unconfirmed from the 8 interviews.
- **Assumption to validate:** Phone-based manual booking (receptionist as the only booking channel) may function as a competing "solution" even inside clinics that had no software at all.

---

## Switching Triggers

The specific moments that converted passive dissatisfaction into active search and purchase.

### Trigger 1 — The Embarrassment Event
> *"Double bookings embarrassed us in front of clients."*

A public failure with a real client present. This is a **social identity threat**, not just an operational inconvenience. It creates urgency because the manager's competence is visible to others. Onboarding messaging should acknowledge this moment explicitly.

### Trigger 2 — Demand Overload
> *"Our phones never stopped ringing."*

Volume crossed a threshold where the reception desk could no longer handle calls while also providing in-clinic service. This is a **capacity constraint**, not a preference. It forces action because the status quo is actively harming the client experience.

### Trigger 3 — Work-Life Boundary Collapse
> *"I wanted my evenings back."*

The shared spreadsheet followed managers home. The trigger here is **personal cost accumulation** — the realisation that the workaround had consumed time that was not meant to be work time. This is the most emotionally loaded trigger and the most potent for retention messaging post-switch.

---

## Identified Gaps in Current Research

The 8 interviews are a strong start, but the following are **unknown and should be validated**:

1. **What other software was considered before Pawpath?** No competing SaaS products were named. Without this, Pawpath cannot benchmark its conversion advantages or anticipate objections.
2. **Who else has a vote in the purchase?** Clinic owners vs. practice managers vs. head vets — the decision-maker and the job-sufferer may not be the same person.
3. **What does "success" look like at 90 days?** No post-switch outcome data was collected. Retention and expansion depend on whether the hired job was actually completed.
4. **What almost prevented the switch?** Price, IT concerns, data migration, staff resistance — none of these friction points were captured and they are critical for onboarding flow design.
5. **Are there clinics who evaluated Pawpath and did not switch?** Understanding the lost deals surfaces unmet hiring criteria or disqualifying weaknesses.

---

## Prioritized Next Steps

Ordered by impact on the stated goals: sharper messaging and improved onboarding flow.

**1. Rewrite the hero message around the three switching triggers** *(High impact / Low effort)*
Replace feature-led copy with trigger-led copy. Lead with the embarrassment and overload moments. Example: *"No more double bookings. No more evenings at the spreadsheet."* Both phrases map directly to confirmed triggers.

**2. Build the onboarding flow around the paper+spreadsheet migrant** *(High impact / Medium effort)*
6 of 8 switchers came from paper + shared spreadsheet. The onboarding must treat this as the default prior state: import existing appointments, retire the spreadsheet on day one, and celebrate the first successful self-booking as a milestone. Do not assume any prior software familiarity.

**3. Conduct 4–6 additional interviews focused on gaps** *(High impact / Medium effort)*
Prioritise: (a) clinics that evaluated but did not purchase, (b) clinics with a multi-person decision process, and (c) clinics that churned. Target completion within 6 weeks to feed the next messaging iteration.

**4. Add a "moments of doubt" question to the onboarding survey** *(Medium impact / Low effort)*
Ask every new clinic: *"What almost stopped you from switching?"* This surfaces friction data at scale with zero additional research cost and directly informs objection handling in sales and onboarding copy.

**5. Define and instrument a "job done" metric** *(Medium impact / Medium effort)*
Assumption to validate: a measurable proxy for "job completed" could be zero double bookings in the first 30 days + at least one self-booking received outside clinic hours. Instrument both events and use them as the activation milestone in onboarding communications. Without a job-done metric, feature adoption data will mislead retention decisions.

---

*Analysis based on 8 clinic manager interviews provided by the Pawpath product team. All figures cited reflect interview data as reported. Figures labelled "Assumption" are hypotheses to be validated.*

# Pawpath SMS Reminders Launch Risks

**Risk Register | FMEA Framework | Date: 2026-10-15 | Owner: TBD**

Pawpath faces a hard-deadline migration of SMS reminders to a new vendor by 30 November — a 6-week window with compounding risk factors: an untested vendor throughput ceiling, two regions requiring 3–4 weeks of sender-ID registration, a single engineer holding all messaging knowledge, and a support environment already under stress (missed-reminder tickets doubled last month). Any one of these conditions would warrant close monitoring; together, they create correlated failure paths that could leave some or all of 410 clinics unable to send reminders on day one of the new contract.

---

Scoring scale — **Severity (S) 1–5 · Likelihood (L) 1–5 · Score = S × L**

| ID | Risk Title | S | L | Score | Priority |
|----|-----------|---|---|-------|----------|
| **R-01** | Sender-ID registration misses cutover deadline for 2 regions | 5 | 4 | **20** | 🔴 Critical |
| **R-02** | Single messaging engineer unavailable during cutover | 5 | 3 | **15** | 🔴 Critical |
| **R-03** | Vendor throughput failure under peak load | 4 | 3 | **12** | 🟠 High |

| **R-09** | Regulatory non-compliance with new sender IDs (TCPA/other) | 4 | 2 | **8** | 🟡 Medium |
| **R-10** | Clinics unaware of sender-ID changes; patients block messages | 3 | 3 | **9** | 🟡 Medium |

## FMEA Deep-Dive: Critical & High Risks

### R-01 — Sender-ID Registration Delay (Score: 20)

| FMEA Dimension | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Failure Mode** | 3–4 week registration process not initiated immediately; bureaucratic delays push approval past 30 Nov |
| **Effect** | Clinics in 2 regions send zero reminders from day 1; patient no-shows increase |
| **Detection (D)** | 2 — registration status is easy to track if monitored daily |
| **RPN (S×L×D)** | 5 × 4 × 2 = **40** |

**Mitigation:**
- **Owner:** Engineering Lead + Vendor Account Manager
- **Action:** Submit sender-ID registration applications for both regions **by 2026-10-19** (Day 4). Treat this as the single most urgent action in the project.
- **Contingency:** Negotiate with new vendor to use a shared short-code or toll-free number as a temporary fallback for those 2 regions while dedicated sender IDs are processed.
- **Monitoring:** Daily status check with vendor; escalation path defined if no approval by Week 4 (2026-11-12).

---

### R-02 — Single Engineer as Single Point of Failure (Score: 15)

| FMEA Dimension | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Failure Mode** | The one messaging engineer is sick, on leave, or leaves the company during the 6-week window |
| **Effect** | Migration halts; no one can troubleshoot outages, configure the new API, or execute rollback procedures |
| **Detection (D)** | 4 — absence is obvious but damage is immediate with no backup |
| **RPN (S×L×D)** | 5 × 3 × 4 = **60** |

**Mitigation:**
- **Owner:** Engineering Manager
- **Action by 2026-10-22:** Conduct 2 knowledge-transfer sessions. Document all messaging system architecture, API credentials, and runbooks in a shared wiki.
- **Action by 2026-10-29:** Cross-train at least one additional engineer to handle the new vendor's API and deployment pipeline.
- **Policy:** Engineer takes no PTO during the final 2 weeks (2026-11-16–30). Confirm vendor provides 24/7 emergency support with a named contact.

### R-03 — Vendor Throughput Failure Under Peak Load (Score: 12)

| FMEA Dimension | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Failure Mode** | Vendor has not been tested above 20,000 messages/hour; batch sends or morning peaks cause message queuing, delays, or drops |
| **Effect** | Reminders arrive late or not at all; patient appointment adherence drops; clinic trust erodes |
| **Detection (D)** | 3 — delivery latency alerts can catch this quickly if monitoring exists |
| **RPN (S×L×D)** | 4 × 3 × 3 = **36** |

- **Owner:** Engineer + Vendor Solutions Architect
- **Action by 2026-10-29:** Run a load test simulating Assumption: peak morning batch (estimated TBD — PM to confirm worst-case hourly volume from current vendor logs). Require vendor written SLA on throughput before cutover.

| FMEA Dimension | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Failure Mode** | New vendor fails critically post-cutover; old contract is terminated |
| **Effect** | Total SMS outage for 410 clinics with no fast recovery path |
| **Detection (D)** | 1 — outage is immediately visible |
| **RPN** | 5 × 2 × 1 = **10** |

**Mitigation:**
- **Owner:** PM + Procurement
- **Action by 2026-10-22:** Evaluate a secondary emergency SMS vendor (e.g., configure a backup account with a different provider) as a cold standby requiring Assumption: <4 hours to activate. Pre-negotiate terms now.

### R-05 — Pre-Existing Failures Masking Post-Migration Issues (Score: 12)

**Failure Mode:** Support tickets about missed reminders already doubled last month. Post-migration, it will be unclear whether failures stem from the new vendor or pre-existing bugs.

**Mitigation:**
- **Owner:** Support Lead + Engineer
- **Action by 2026-10-22:** Investigate and document the root cause of current missed reminders. Establish a clear pre-migration failure-rate baseline (count and category).
- **Action:** Tag all new-vendor-routed messages in logs from cutover day so failures can be attributed correctly.

### R-06 — Clinic Configuration / Data Migration Errors (Score: 12)

**Mitigation:**
- **Owner:** Engineer + QA

# Pawpath North Star

Pawpath's retention data reveals a clear activation threshold: clinics that confirm at least 80% of their appointments through Pawpath reminders renew at a materially higher rate than those that do not, yet today only 52% of booked appointments are confirmed via the platform. This document defines the single metric that best captures the value Pawpath delivers to clinics and pet owners, identifies the operational levers the team can move, and translates them into a prioritized growth roadmap. Closing the gap between 52% and 80% is not just a product goal — it is the most direct path to protecting and compounding recurring revenue.

---

## North Star Metric

### **Appointment Confirmation Rate via Pawpath**
*The percentage of all booked appointments across active clinics that receive a confirmed response through a Pawpath-delivered reminder.*

**Current baseline:** 52%
**Why this metric, not another:**

- **It reflects value to both sides of the marketplace.** A confirmed appointment means the clinic has near-certainty a chair is filled and can plan staffing accordingly; the pet owner has acknowledged the visit and is less likely to miss care for their animal.
- **It is the proven retention signal.** Pawpath's own data links the ≥80% threshold to significantly higher renewal rates — this metric is therefore simultaneously a product health signal and a leading revenue indicator.
- **The team can move it.** Every lever below (reminder delivery, clinic ingestion, response behavior) is within the product and go-to-market team's control.
- **It is unambiguous.** "Confirmed via Pawpath" has a binary outcome per appointment, making measurement, accountability, and debugging straightforward.

**What it is not:** Total appointments booked, total revenue, or a satisfaction score. Those are either lagging outcomes or too indirect to drive daily decision-making.

---

## Input Metrics

These are the 5 levers whose collective improvement moves the North Star.

### 1. Clinic Appointment Ingestion Rate
**Definition:** % of a clinic's total booked appointments that are entered into Pawpath (manually, via integration, or via import).

**Why it matters:** This is the ceiling of the North Star. If a clinic only enters 60% of appointments into Pawpath, the confirmation rate can never exceed 60% for that clinic — regardless of how well reminders perform. This is likely a silent depressor of the current 52% baseline.

**Assumption to validate:** A portion of the gap between 52% and 80% may be explained entirely by incomplete appointment ingestion rather than reminder performance.

### 2. Reminder Delivery Rate
**Definition:** % of sent reminders that are successfully delivered (not bounced, blocked, or undelivered) across all active channels (SMS, email, app push).

**Why it matters:** Undelivered reminders produce zero confirmations. Deliverability issues — stale phone numbers, spam filters, carrier blocks — are invisible unless actively tracked. A Target: 95%+ delivery rate should be the floor; anything below this silently suppresses the NSM.

### 3. Pet Owner Response Rate
**Definition:** % of successfully delivered reminders that receive a confirmation (or cancellation) reply within the reminder window.

**Why it matters:** This is the core engagement metric — it measures whether Pawpath's reminder experience is compelling enough to prompt action. Low response rates indicate issues with timing, channel preference, message copy, or confirmation UX friction.

### 4. Multi-Channel Reachability per Pet Owner Contact
**Definition:** % of pet owner contact records with at least two valid, active channels (e.g., SMS + email, or email + app).

**Why it matters:** Single-channel contacts represent a single point of failure. If that channel fails (number changed, email bounced), the reminder never lands. Building redundancy into contact profiles is a structural improvement to delivery and response rates.

### 5. New Clinic Activation Rate (60-Day)
**Definition:** % of newly onboarded clinics that reach ≥80% appointment confirmation rate within their first 60 days.

**Why it matters:** Clinics that hit the activation threshold early are more likely to sustain it and renew. This metric identifies whether onboarding sets clinics up for success or leaves them to figure it out independently — and it is a leading indicator of future NSM health. **Assumption:** 60 days is a reasonable activation window; validate against actual time-to-first-confirmation data.

---

## Counter Metrics

These metrics ensure the team does not optimize the North Star at the expense of product health or customer experience.

- **Pet Owner Opt-Out Rate** — Aggressive reminder cadences or poorly timed messages may inflate short-term response rates while eroding the reachable contact base. If opt-outs rise as response rate rises, the strategy is unsustainable.
- **False Confirmation Rate** — % of "confirmed" appointments that still result in a no-show. If this rises, the NSM becomes a vanity metric disconnected from actual clinic value. Track confirmed-but-no-showed as a separate signal.
- **Clinic Support Ticket Volume (Reminder-Related)** — A rising NSM alongside rising support tickets may signal that the confirmation workflow is becoming burdensome for clinic staff.
- **Clinic Churn Rate** — The ultimate lagging counter metric. If NSM improves but churn does not fall within two quarters, revisit whether the 80% threshold is the correct activation signal or whether other factors (pricing, competition, clinic size) are confounding the renewal data.

---

## Targets

| Metric | Current | Target (12-month) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Appointment Confirmation Rate (NSM)** | **52%** | **Target: 70%** | Stretch: 75%. Assumption: achievable without major platform rebuild |
| Clinics at ≥80% confirmation rate | TBD — measure immediately | **Target: 50% of active clinics** | Baseline unknown; establish within 30 days |
| Clinic Appointment Ingestion Rate | TBD | **Target: 90%+** | Assumption: currently below 85% for many clinics |
| Reminder Delivery Rate | TBD | **Target: 95%+** | Assumption: currently unmeasured |
| Pet Owner Response Rate | TBD | **Target: 65%+** | Assumption: currently unmeasured |
| New Clinic 60-Day Activation Rate | TBD | **Target: 70% of new clinics** | Assumption: currently below 50% |

---

## Initiatives Mapped to Input Metrics

### Ingestion Rate
- **EHR/PMS integrations:** Build or deepen integrations with the top 3 practice management systems used by current clinics — this automates appointment sync and eliminates manual entry as a bottleneck. **Assumption:** identify top PMS platforms from clinic survey; currently unknown.
- **Bulk import and sync audit:** Surface a "missing appointments" alert in the clinic dashboard when Pawpath detects fewer appointments than expected based on historical patterns.

### Reminder Delivery Rate
- **Contact hygiene workflow:** Prompt clinics (or pet owners) to validate/update contact details at check-in or via a periodic verification reminder.
- **Channel fallback logic:** Automatically retry a failed SMS reminder via email within a defined window (e.g., Assumption: 2 hours before the reminder deadline).

### Pet Owner Response Rate
- **Reminder timing optimization:** A/B test sending reminders at 72 hours, 48 hours, and 24 hours before appointments to find peak response windows.
- **One-tap confirmation UX:** Reduce confirmation to a single tap from the reminder message — no login, no form. Measure response rate before and after.
- **Message copy refresh:** Test plain-language, pet-personalized copy (using pet name, appointment type) against generic templates.

### Multi-Channel Reachability
- **Dual-channel enrollment nudge:** During new patient registration flow (clinic-side), surface a prompt requiring at least two contact methods before the record is marked complete.
- **Pawpath pet owner app:** **Expert recommendation (gap identified):** If a native app does not exist, a lightweight pet owner app with push notifications would add a zero-cost, high-reliability third channel. This is a medium-term initiative.

### New Clinic Activation Rate
- **Structured onboarding playbook:** Create a 4-week activation program with milestone check-ins at day 7, 14, and 30. The program ends only when the clinic crosses 80% confirmation rate for one full week.
- **In-app activation dashboard:** Give clinics real-time visibility into their own confirmation rate vs. the 80% threshold, with guided recommendations to close the gap.

---

## Identified Gaps & Expert Analysis

The PM's input is directionally strong but leaves several unknowns that must be resolved before the team commits to targets:

1. **Root cause of the 52% baseline is unknown.** The NSM could be suppressed by ingestion gaps, delivery failures, or low response rates — or all three. A diagnostic breakdown (ingestion × delivery × response) should be run immediately. This changes which input metric to prioritize first.
2. **The renewal rate differential is unquantified.** Knowing that clinics at ≥80% renew at a "much higher rate" is compelling, but the team should quantify the delta (e.g., Assumption: 30–40 percentage points higher renewal — validate against internal cohort data). This number is the business case for every initiative above.
3. **Clinic segmentation is missing.** Small single-vet practices and large multi-location clinics likely have very different ingestion and activation patterns. Segmented NSM targets may be needed.
4. **Pet owner channel preferences are unknown.** Building multi-channel reachability without knowing whether pet owners prefer SMS vs. email vs. app is guesswork. A short survey or response-rate analysis by channel should precede channel investment decisions.

---

## Prioritized Next Steps

1. **[Week 1–2] Diagnose the 52% baseline.** Decompose current confirmation rate into: appointments ingested ÷ booked × delivered reminders ÷ ingested × confirmations ÷ delivered. This single analysis tells you where the biggest lever is.
2. **[Week 2–4] Establish missing baselines.** Instrument and begin tracking Ingestion Rate, Delivery Rate, Response Rate, and False Confirmation Rate. You cannot manage what you do not measure.
3. **[Month 1–2] Quantify the renewal rate gap.** Pull a cohort analysis comparing renewal rates for clinics above and below 80% confirmation rate. Attach a dollar figure to closing the gap — this becomes the internal business case for resourcing initiatives.
4. **[Month 2–3] Ship one-tap confirmation UX.** Lowest-friction, highest-impact improvement to Response Rate. No integration dependency; ships fast.

# Positioning Pawpath

Pawpath sits in a genuinely defensible position: it is the only appointment tool built around how veterinary medicine actually works — species-specific time requirements and treatment-driven follow-up — while remaining light enough for a small independent clinic to adopt in a single afternoon. The three alternatives clinics currently rely on (paper diaries, salon-derived booking tools, and the scheduling module inside a large practice-management suite) each fail on at least two of those three dimensions. The strongest signal in the input is that **customers say reminders are the reason they stay** — meaning retention is already anchored to the most differentiated feature, which is exactly where positioning should point.

---

## Step 1 — Competitive Alternatives

What independent vet clinics (2–8 vets) actually do today instead of using Pawpath:

- **Paper diaries** — zero software cost, fully flexible, but no automated follow-up, no utilization visibility, and error-prone when a locum or receptionist covers.
- **Generic salon booking tools** — cloud-based, familiar UI, but built around "service + duration" logic for humans. They have no concept of species, no treatment context, and reminders are time-based rather than clinically driven.
- **Scheduling module inside a large practice-management suite** — vet-aware in principle, but the scheduling piece is bundled with billing, dispensing, and records. For a 2–8 vet independent clinic, the suite is over-specified, expensive, and typically takes weeks to implement. Many clinics buy it and only use 20–30% of it (Assumption: placeholder — validate with clinic interviews).

**Expert note:** The large-suite alternative is the most important to neutralize in messaging. Clinics that have been burned by a failed suite implementation are primed for Pawpath's "one afternoon" setup story.

---

## Step 2 — Unique Attributes

Features Pawpath has that the alternatives do not, or cannot easily replicate:

- **Species-aware visit lengths** — appointment slots are configured by species (and implicitly by visit type), not by a flat duration the clinic guesses at. A feline dental and a canine vaccination do not get the same 20-minute block.
- **Recheck reminders tied to the treatment given** — the trigger for a reminder is clinical (what was done), not calendrical (how many days since the last visit). A post-surgical recheck fires differently than a routine vaccine reminder.
- **One-afternoon setup** — not a selling point about simplicity for its own sake, but a direct counter to the "implementation risk" that makes small clinics avoid software entirely or stay stuck on paper.

---

## Step 3 — Value Enabled

What those attributes actually deliver for the clinic owner and their staff:

| Attribute | Operational value | Business value |
|---|---|---|
| Species-aware visit lengths | Accurate daily schedule; fewer overruns and gaps | Higher chair utilization without adding staff |
| Treatment-tied reminders | Pets come back at the clinically right time | Increased return visits; stronger patient compliance record |
| One-afternoon setup | No disruption to a running clinic | Near-zero adoption risk; immediate ROI start date |

**The reminders insight is critical.** When customers say reminders are why they stay, they are describing a switching cost — not just a feature preference. Reminders that are tied to treatment are sticky because they embed Pawpath into the clinical workflow, not just the front-desk workflow. This is the core of the retention moat.

---

## Step 4 — Target Customers Who Care Most

Not all independent vet clinics are equal buyers. The highest-value initial segment shares these characteristics:

- **Practice size:** 2–8 vets (as specified). Large enough to have scheduling complexity; small enough that a full suite is overkill.
- **Current situation:** On paper diaries or a salon tool they know is wrong for them. Clinics already on a large suite and happy are a harder conversion.
- **Trigger event:** A missed recheck, a complaint about no follow-up, a no-show pattern that the owner is losing sleep over, or a new practice manager hired to "sort out the admin."
- **Decision maker:** The practice owner or senior vet, who feels the clinical consequence of poor follow-up, not just the scheduling friction.
- **Emotional posture:** Frustrated that their software "doesn't understand how a vet clinic works." This exact phrase, or something close to it, is the psychographic signal to listen for.

**Secondary segment to watch:** Multi-site groups of 2–3 independent clinics that have outgrown paper but are not ready for a full practice-management platform. (Assumption: requires validation — Pawpath's current feature set may or may not support multi-site.)

---

## Step 5 — Market Category

**Recommended category: Veterinary Appointment Software**

**Why not "practice management software"?** That category immediately invites comparison to large suites. Pawpath loses on features in that fight even if it wins on fit.

**Why not "booking software" or "scheduling software"?** Too broad. It puts Pawpath next to salon tools and Calendly in the prospect's mental shortlist, which dilutes the vet-specific differentiation.

**"Veterinary appointment software"** does three things:
1. Filters the audience (only vet clinics read past the first word).
2. Sets a scope expectation (appointments, not the whole clinical record) — which is honest and reduces over-promise risk.
3. Creates a category where Pawpath can be the default reference point rather than a challenger to an established giant.

---

## Positioning Statement

> **For independent vet clinics with 2–8 vets** that are losing patients between visits and wasting chair time on appointment slots that don't match how animals are actually treated, **Pawpath** is **veterinary appointment software** that schedules by species and reminds clients based on what their pet received — not just the date. Unlike paper diaries, salon booking tools, or the scheduling add-on buried inside a large practice suite, Pawpath is built exclusively around how a small vet practice works and is live the same afternoon you start.

---

## Gaps & Expert Analysis

The following are unresolved questions that will sharpen or break this positioning as Pawpath grows. Each should be treated as a research or validation task.

### Gap 1 — No quantified retention or reminder impact
Customers say reminders are why they stay, but there is no metric attached. **Action:** Interview 5–10 retained customers and ask: "Before Pawpath, what percentage of recommended rechecks were actually booked?" Compare to their estimate now. Even directional numbers transform the sales story from anecdote to evidence.

### Gap 2 — No pricing signal
Positioning affects price anchoring. If Pawpath is priced against salon tools, it looks expensive. If anchored against the scheduling module cost inside a large suite, it looks like a bargain with faster setup. **Action:** Define the pricing anchor explicitly in sales collateral — this is a positioning decision, not just a pricing decision.

### Gap 3 — Integration posture is undefined
Many clinics on large suites still use the suite for records and billing. Does Pawpath replace the scheduling module only, or does it sit alongside? If it can coexist, the "already have a suite" clinic becomes an addressable segment. If not, that segment is off-limits and messaging should actively exclude it to avoid wasted sales cycles. (Assumption: this is undefined — confirm with engineering.)

### Gap 4 — "One afternoon" claim needs a proof mechanism
This is a powerful differentiator but a claim that skeptical buyers will challenge. **Action:** Document the setup steps, create a short video of a real clinic going live, and add a setup-time guarantee or SLA to the trial experience.

### Gap 5 — The "reminders" retention insight is not yet in the positioning
Currently the attributes lead with scheduling; reminders are listed second. But if reminders are the retention driver, they should lead the narrative. Consider reordering: lead with "never lose a patient between visits," then support it with the scheduling accuracy story.

---

## Prioritized Next Steps

1. **Validate the retention claim (highest priority)** — Interview 5–10 current customers specifically about recheck rates and reminder impact. This turns the positioning's strongest claim from qualitative to defensible.

2. **Reorder the narrative** — Update website, sales deck, and one-pagers to lead with treatment-tied reminders ("never lose a patient between visits"), then land scheduling accuracy as the supporting story.

3. **Define the pricing anchor** — Decide whether Pawpath is positioned against salon-tool pricing or suite-module pricing. Build that anchor into the first page of every sales conversation.

4. **Clarify the integration posture** — Determine and document whether Pawpath coexists with an existing suite or replaces it. This gates whether the "already on a suite" segment is in or out of the ICP.

5. **Proof the "one afternoon" claim** — Create a setup walkthrough (video or step-by-step guide) that makes this claim viscerally credible before a buyer has to trust it on faith.

6. **Test the market category label** — Run the phrase "veterinary appointment software" past 3–5 target clinic owners. Ask: "If you were searching for a tool like this, what would you type?" Adjust the category name to match actual search language while preserving the vet-specific filter.

# Reminder Send-Time A/B Test Design

**Pawpath | Prepared by: [account email from CLI context] | Date: 2026-10-15**

This document designs a rigorous experiment to determine whether shifting recheck reminder send-time from 3 days to 7 days before the appointment due date meaningfully improves rebooking rates above the current baseline of 69%. The test will run for **3 calendar months** using **clinic-level randomization** across all 410 clinics, with a pre-registered primary metric, guardrail metrics, and a single interim analysis. Two critical gaps — the minimum detectable effect the business accepts and the empirical intra-cluster correlation — must be resolved before launch, as they drive the entire duration calculation.

---

## Hypothesis

**If** recheck reminders are sent 7 days before the appointment due date instead of 3 days, **then** the rebooking rate will increase above the current 69% **because** pet owners require a sufficient planning horizon to coordinate veterinary visits into household schedules, and a 3-day window is too short for a meaningful share of owners to act.

---

## Experiment Design

### Control (A)
Single recheck reminder sent **3 days before** the appointment due date — current production behavior.

### Treatment (B)
Single recheck reminder sent **7 days before** the appointment due date.

**Scope boundary:** This test isolates send-day offset only. It does **not** test a dual-reminder strategy (7-day + 3-day follow-up), which is a natural follow-up experiment if Treatment wins.

---

## Randomization Unit

**Recommendation: Clinic-level (cluster) randomization**

- Clinics vary significantly in size, creating confounding risk under individual-level randomization
- Clinic staff experience a consistent reminder cadence within their clinic, preventing workflow contamination (e.g., staff adapting scheduling behavior when they see mixed lead times)
- Avoids SUTVA violations for multi-pet households whose pets would otherwise land in both arms

**Stratification:** Pre-stratify the 410 clinics into size tiers (small / medium / large — **Assumption:** define tiers using Pawpath's internal clinic segmentation) before random assignment, ensuring balance across arms. Use a 50/50 split: **205 clinics per arm.**

**Alternative considered:** Individual reminder-level randomization achieves required sample size ~4× faster (see Duration) but risks within-clinic contamination. Escalate to engineering and operations for a feasibility ruling if 3-month duration is unacceptable.

---

## Metrics

### Primary Metric
**Rebooking rate** — proportion of reminders resulting in a confirmed recheck booking before the appointment due date.

*Baseline: 69% (PM input)*

> ⚠️ **Gap — measurement window:** The 7-day arm has 4 extra days of potential conversion time vs. the 3-day arm if rebooking is simply measured from send-date to due-date. **Resolution required before launch:** Either (a) measure rebooking within a fixed 3-day window post-reminder for both arms, or (b) use "appointment kept" as the long-run outcome. Pre-register the chosen definition.

### Guardrail Metrics

| Metric | Direction to Flag |
|---|---|
| Cancellation rate post-rebook | Increase in Treatment — earlier bookings may be more tentative |
| No-show rate | Increase in Treatment — longer gap increases forgetting |
| Reminder opt-out / unsubscribe rate | Increase in Treatment — 7-day reminder may feel premature |
| Clinic appointment capacity utilization | Asymmetric clustering in either arm |
| Support contacts re: reminder confusion | Spike in either arm |

---

## Sample Size & Power

### Inputs
- **Baseline rate (p₁):** 69%
- **Assumption — MDE:** +2 percentage points (69% → 71%), representing ~2.9% relative improvement. **PM must validate this threshold** — accepting a 3pp MDE shortens duration by ~1 month.
- Two-sided test, α = 0.05, power = 80%
- **Assumption — ICC:** 0.05 (moderate clinic-level homogeneity in rebooking behavior). **Validate against historical clinic-level data before launch** — this is the single most impactful assumption.

### Calculation

**Step 1 — Raw per-arm sample size (no clustering):**

Using two-proportion z-test with p₁ = 0.69, p₂ = 0.71:
**n ≈ 8,250 reminders per arm**

**Step 2 — Cluster Design Effect:**
- Average reminders per clinic per month: 24,000 ÷ 410 ≈ **58.5**
- Design Effect (DEFF) = 1 + (58.5 − 1) × 0.05 = **3.88**
- Adjusted n per arm = 8,250 × 3.88 ≈ **32,000 reminders**

**Total reminders required: ~64,000**

---

## Expected Duration

**Recommended run: 3 full calendar months**

- 64,000 total reminders needed ÷ 24,000/month = 2.67 months → round up to **3 months** for buffer and to capture complete monthly scheduling cycles
- Start on the **first of a calendar month**; end exactly 3 months later for clean cohort definition
- Avoid spanning a major holiday boundary; adjust start date accordingly

**If individual-level randomization is approved:** 8,250 per arm ÷ 12,000/month per arm = 0.69 months → minimum **4-week** run to capture full weekly cycles

---

## Analysis Plan

### Pre-Registration
Lock the full analysis plan — hypothesis, metrics, subgroups, decision rules — in the experiment management system **before any data is collected.** No modifications after unblinding.

### Primary Analysis
**Mixed-effects logistic regression** with clinic as a random effect.
- Covariates: clinic size stratum, calendar month, clinic tenure on Pawpath
- Outcome: binary rebooking flag per reminder
- Report odds ratio + 95% CI; convert to percentage-point difference for stakeholder communication

### Pre-Specified Subgroup Analyses
1. **Clinic size (small / medium / large)** — highest priority given stated size variation; check for heterogeneous treatment effect
2. **Day of week reminder is sent** — Monday–Wednesday vs. Thursday–Sunday may show differential response
3. **Pet owner tenure** — new vs. returning Pawpath users (if available)
4. **Recheck type** — first recheck vs. follow-up (if available)

### Interim Analysis
One pre-specified interim at **Week 6** (halfway), using **O'Brien-Fleming alpha-spending** to allow early stopping only for extreme effects. No other data peeks. Communicate this policy to all stakeholders before launch.

### Decision Rules

| Outcome | Decision |
|---|---|
| Treatment significantly better (p < 0.05, CI above 0pp) | Roll out 7-day reminder to all clinics |
| No significant difference | Maintain 3-day send; test dual-reminder strategy next |
| Treatment significantly worse | Do not rollout; conduct qualitative owner research |
| Any guardrail breached | Hold decision; investigate before acting on primary metric |

---

## Potential Pitfalls

### 🚨 Simpson's Paradox — High Risk
Large clinics generate a disproportionate share of the 24,000 monthly reminders. If randomization doesn't balance clinic sizes across arms, aggregate rebooking rates can mislead directionally.
**Mitigation:** Pre-stratified randomization by clinic size tier; clinic size as regression covariate.

### ⚠️ Measurement Window Asymmetry — High Risk
The 7-day arm has 4 more days of potential conversion time if rebooking is measured from send-date to due-date. This would artificially inflate Treatment's rate.
**Mitigation:** Pre-register a consistent measurement window definition before launch (see Metrics gap above).

### ⚠️ Novelty Effect — Low Risk (but Monitor)
Pet owners are unaware of the test, so novelty is minimal. However, **clinic staff** may behave differently when they notice a timing change.
**Mitigation:** Monitor for abnormal appointment-scheduling patterns in the first 2 weeks post-launch.

### ⚠️ Seasonality Carry-Over
Reminders sent in month 1 may generate appointments in month 2. Cohort definition must be based on **reminder send-date**, not appointment date.

### ⚠️ Dual-Reminder Confound
A "7 days only" win does not rule out that the optimal strategy is "7 days + 3 days." Plan a follow-up test explicitly.

---

## Open Questions & Gaps

1. **What MDE does leadership accept?** The +2pp assumption is the largest lever on experiment duration. Confirm before any engineering scoping.
2. **How is rebooking currently instrumented?** Confirm the measurement event, window, and attribution logic before building test tracking.
3. **What is the historical clinic-level ICC?** Pull clinic-level rebooking rates from the past 6 months to empirically replace the 0.05 assumption. One week of analytics work could save or add a month of test duration.
4. **What time of day are reminders currently sent?** Send time-of-day may interact with the send-day offset and should be held constant across arms.
5. **Do clinics already customize reminder timing?** If yes, control-arm behavior may be inconsistent and must be normalized before test launch.

---

## Prioritized Next Steps

1. **[PM + Analytics — This week]** Pull historical clinic-level rebooking rates to empirically estimate ICC; confirm the +2pp MDE with leadership. These two inputs determine whether the experiment is 4 weeks or 3 months.
2. **[PM — This week]** Define and document the rebooking measurement window; get sign-off from Analytics and Product before any instrumentation work begins.
3. **[Engineering + Analytics — Weeks 2–3]** Pre-register the full analysis plan; build stratified randomization logic using clinic size tiers.
4. **[PM + Operations — Before launch]** Brief clinic operations teams; establish guardrail metric dashboards with automated alerts for cancellation rate, no-show rate, and opt-outs.
5. **[Analytics — Week 6]** Execute the pre-specified interim analysis under O'Brien-Fleming boundaries. No other data reviews until the scheduled interim.
6. **[PM — Post-test]** If 7-day send wins, immediately design the follow-up dual-reminder (7-day + 3-day) experiment to test whether an additional nudge compound the gain.

# Pawpath Waitlist — User Stories

**Prepared by:** [account name from CLI context] | **Date:** 2026-10-15 | **Framework:** INVEST + Gherkin

---

Pawpath's current paper waitlist forces front-desk staff to make manual phone calls whenever an appointment slot is freed — a slow, error-prone process that leaves slots unfilled and owners frustrated. This document defines a complete set of user stories for an **automated SMS-based waitlist** that instantly offers freed slots to the first eligible pet owner, holds the slot for **15 minutes**, and cascades to the next owner on no-response. Stories are grouped by epic, prioritized by delivery risk, and supplemented with expert gap analysis and actionable recommendations.

---

## Epic 1: Waitlist Registration

*Pet owners self-enrol; staff can also enrol on their behalf.*

---

### Story 1.1 — Owner Self-Enrolment on Waitlist

**As a** pet owner, **I want** to add myself to the waitlist for a specific clinic, service, and preferred time window, **so that** I am automatically notified if a matching slot becomes available without having to call the clinic.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

```gherkin
Given I am a registered Pawpath user with at least one pet profile
When I navigate to a clinic's booking page and all slots are full
Then I see a "Join Waitlist" option for that clinic and service type

Given I tap "Join Waitlist"
When I select my preferred time window (e.g., weekday mornings) and submit
Then I receive an SMS confirmation: "You're #[position] on the waitlist for [Clinic] — [Service]"
And my entry is stored with a UTC timestamp for FIFO ordering

Given I attempt to join the same clinic/service waitlist twice
When I submit the second request
Then I see an error: "You're already on this waitlist at position #[N]"
And no duplicate entry is created
```

---

### Story 1.2 — Staff Enrolment on Owner's Behalf

**As a** front-desk staff member, **I want** to add a pet owner to the waitlist from the clinic dashboard, **so that** owners who call in can be enrolled without needing the mobile app.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

```gherkin
Given I am logged in as front-desk staff
When I search for an owner by name or phone number and select "Add to Waitlist"
Then I can choose the service type, preferred time window, and pet
And the owner receives an SMS: "You've been added to the waitlist at [Clinic] by staff"

Given the owner's phone number has not opted in to SMS
When I attempt to add them
Then the system displays a warning: "SMS consent required — obtain verbal consent and check the consent box to proceed"
And enrolment is blocked until the box is checked
```

---

## Epic 2: Slot Offer & Confirmation

*Core value delivery — the automated cascade.*

---

### Story 2.1 — Automatic SMS Offer on Slot Release

**As a** pet owner on the waitlist, **I want** to receive an SMS the moment a matching slot is freed, **so that** I can claim the appointment before anyone else.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

```gherkin
Given an appointment is cancelled at [Clinic] for [Service] on [Date/Time]
When the system identifies that at least one waitlisted owner's preferred window matches
Then an SMS is sent to the first matching owner within 60 seconds of cancellation
And the SMS reads: "A slot opened at [Clinic] on [Date] at [Time] for [Service]. Reply YES to book or NO to skip. Offer expires in 15 minutes."
And the slot status is set to "on-hold"

Given no waitlisted owner matches the freed slot's service type or time window
When the system checks the waitlist
Then the slot is released back to public booking immediately
And front-desk staff receive an in-app alert: "Slot freed — no waitlist match found"
```

---

### Story 2.2 — Owner Accepts the Slot Offer

**As a** pet owner, **I want** to confirm a slot by replying YES to an SMS, **so that** my appointment is booked instantly without opening the app.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

```gherkin
Given I received a slot offer SMS and the 15-minute hold is active
When I reply "YES" (case-insensitive)
Then my appointment is confirmed and I receive: "Booked! [Clinic], [Date], [Time], [Service] for [Pet Name]. Reply CANCEL to cancel."
And I am removed from the waitlist
And the slot status changes from "on-hold" to "confirmed"

Given I reply "YES" after the 15-minute hold has expired
When the system processes my reply
Then I receive: "Sorry, this offer has expired. You've been moved back to position #[N] on the waitlist."
And the slot has already been offered to the next owner
```

---

### Story 2.3 — Cascade on No-Response or Rejection

**As a** clinic manager, **I want** the system to automatically offer the slot to the next eligible owner if the first owner does not respond or declines, **so that** slots are never wasted.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

```gherkin
Given an SMS offer was sent to owner #1 and 15 minutes elapse with no YES reply
When the hold timer expires
Then the slot is offered to owner #2 with a fresh 15-minute hold
And owner #1 receives: "Your offer expired. You remain on the waitlist."

Given owner #1 replies "NO"
When the system receives the reply
Then the slot is immediately offered to owner #2 (no wait for the 15-minute timer)
And owner #1 is removed from the waitlist for that service

Given all waitlisted owners have been offered the slot and none accepted
When the cascade is exhausted
Then the slot is released to public booking
And front-desk staff receive an alert: "Slot unclaimed after full cascade — now public"
```

---

## Epic 3: Waitlist Self-Management (Owner)

---

### Story 3.1 — Owner Views and Leaves Waitlist

**As a** pet owner, **I want** to view my waitlist position and remove myself at any time, **so that** I am not offered slots I no longer need.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

```gherkin
Given I am on the Pawpath app waitlist screen
When I view my active waitlist entries
Then I see clinic name, service, my current position, and date enrolled

Given I tap "Leave Waitlist" for a specific entry
When I confirm the action
Then I am removed immediately
And I receive an SMS: "You've left the waitlist for [Clinic] — [Service]."
And my position is not offered to me; the queue compresses
```

---

## Epic 4: Staff & Manager Tools

---

### Story 4.1 — Front-Desk Views Live Waitlist

**As a** front-desk staff member, **I want** to see the live waitlist for each service with owner names, positions, and offer status, **so that** I can answer owner questions and manually intervene if needed.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

```gherkin
Given I am on the clinic dashboard
When I open the Waitlist panel for a service
Then I see a ranked list: position, owner name, pet name, preferred window, enrolment timestamp
And I can see if a slot offer is currently active (with countdown timer)

Given a slot offer is active and I need to override it
When I click "Cancel Offer & Release Slot"
Then the hold is released, the public slot opens, and the owner receives: "The held slot has been released by the clinic."
```

---

### Story 4.2 — Manager Configures Waitlist Settings

**As a** clinic manager, **I want** to configure the hold duration and SMS quiet hours, **so that** the system respects our clinic's operating policies.

> **Assumption:** Hold duration defaults to **15 minutes** per PM input, but managers may need to adjust (e.g., 10–30 min range). Quiet hours and range limits are **TBD — validate with PM.**

**Acceptance Criteria:**

```gherkin
Given I am logged in as clinic manager
When I open Waitlist Settings
Then I can set hold duration (Assumption: 10–30 minutes, default 15)
And I can set SMS quiet hours (e.g., no SMS before 08:00 or after 20:00 local time)
And I can set a maximum waitlist size per service (Assumption: TBD)

Given quiet hours are active and a slot is freed
When the system attempts to send an SMS offer
Then the offer SMS is queued until quiet hours end
And the slot is held in "pending offer" status until the SMS is sent
```

---

## Expert Gap Analysis

The PM's brief is clear on the trigger and hold mechanic but leaves several **high-risk gaps** unaddressed:

| # | Gap | Risk | Recommendation |
|---|-----|------|----------------|
| 1 | **Matching criteria undefined** | High — cascade logic cannot be built | Define matching: service type + preferred day/time window minimum. Confirm if species, vet preference, or location radius apply. |
| 2 | **SMS opt-in / consent (TCPA/GDPR)** | High — legal/compliance blocker | Require explicit SMS consent at registration; log consent timestamp and method. |
| 3 | **Quiet hours not specified** | Medium — owners receive 2 AM texts | Confirm default quiet hours with PM; add manager config (Story 4.2). |
